title: Theory of Mind incommitted patients with schizophrenia in forensic psychiatry—Identification of risk factors for improved relapse prevention
summary: Theory of Mind (ToM) describes the ability to recognize mental states such as thoughts, emotions, or intentions in oneself and others—a central prerequisite for successful social interaction. Recent models differentiate between cognitive (inferring intentions) and affective (recognizing emotions) ToM. Studies show that ToM functions are impaired, particularly in schizophrenia, which promotes social misinterpretations and withdrawal. Meta-analyses and neurobiological findings point to fragmented network integration in the brains of those affected. Recent studies with forensic samples also indicate that ToM deficits are a strong predictor of violent behavior—stronger than intelligence or psychiatric diagnosis. This suggests that social cognitive impairments pose an independent risk. Given the limited effectiveness of pharmacological treatments, psychological interventions such as cognitive remediation, which also includes ToM components, are gaining in importance. However, in German-speaking forensic psychiatric institutions, where schizophrenia is a primary diagnosis, there is a lack of empirical data on ToM. The aim of the study is therefore to systematically record ToM deficits in forensic patients with schizophrenia in order to derive specific therapeutic training approaches for promoting social cognition.

interventions.name: As part of the planned diagnostic, non-interventional, cross-sectional study (diagnostic), ToM abilities will be evaluated using standardized instruments. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients who are forensically committed (according to §63 STGB) or
o    Patients of the forensic aftercare outpatient clinic
o    Both competent and incompetent patients (in the latter case, the consent of the legal guardian is also obtained)
o	Main diagnosis F20
o    Male gender
o    Age: 20 years and older •
o    Native language German or sufficient language skills to participate in the neuropsychological examinations
Exclusion criteria:
• Physical illnesses that prevent participation in the study (e.g., bedridden, blindness, deafness)
• Clinically relevant depression PHQ> 9
• Neurological diseases
• Stroke
• History of traumatic brain injury
• History of suicide attempts
